Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java` (mine was the only `*AgentTest.java` in the tree). It's self-contained, uses JUnit 5 (matching the project's existing tests) and covers:

- Constants and the deprecated public no-arg constructor
- `add*` methods (days/hours/minutes/seconds/milliseconds/months/weeks/years), including month-end clamping and null checks
- `ceiling`/`truncate`/`round` for `Date`, `Calendar`, and `Object` overloads, including `SEMI_MONTH`, unsupported-field `IllegalArgumentException`, `ClassCastException`, `ArithmeticException` for huge years, and null checks
- `getFragmentIn{Days,Hours,Minutes,Seconds,Milliseconds}` for both `Calendar`/`Date`, including unsupported fragments and nulls
- `isSameDay`/`isSameInstant`/`isSameLocalTime`
- `iterator` across all range styles (including the exact javadoc month-range example), invalid range styles, `ClassCastException`, exhaustion (`NoSuchElementException`) and `remove()` (`UnsupportedOperationException`)
- `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly` including multi-pattern fallback, leniency rollover vs. strict rejection, and null checks
- `set*` field setters with valid boundaries and out-of-range `IllegalArgumentException`
- `toCalendar`, `toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`
- `truncatedCompareTo`/`truncatedEquals`

All 38 test methods pass via `./_tools/test.sh`, and no other files were modified.
